controls: Sampling is planned at a stack location
Provide safe access to the sampling position.
Personnel will work at the sampling position
Provide a safe place of work.
Provide suitable access for the sampling equipment.
Inability to deploy the required method
Sampling equipment and personnel are deployed
Provide enough working space for both.
The monitoring technique needs site services
Provide required electricity, lighting, water or other essential services.
Sampling failure caused by missing services
Collected analyte mass and sampled gas volume are available
Calculate concentration as collected mass divided by sample volume.
Stack velocity and cross-sectional area are available
Calculate volume flow as velocity multiplied by cross-sectional area.
Concentration and stack volume flow are available
Calculate mass emission rate from concentration multiplied by volume flow.
Concentration is converted to a mass emission rate
Put concentration and flow rate on the same reference conditions before combining them.
A mass emission result is reported
Do not subtract measurement uncertainty from the mass-emission result.
A gaseous result is in ppm but the permit requires mass concentration
Convert using molecular weight and molar volume at the stated reference conditions.
A mass concentration needs standard temperature and pressure
Use the applicable permit conditions, commonly 273 K and 101.3 kPa.
Comparing concentrations at different physical conditions
A measured concentration must be corrected to 273 K
Apply the temperature correction using the measured absolute temperature.
A measured concentration must be corrected to 101.3 kPa
Apply the pressure correction using pressure at the sample-volume measurement point.
Correct wet concentration to dry basis using the measured water percentage.
The permit specifies a reference oxygen level
Correct the measured concentration to the permit oxygen reference.
Maintain a monitoring strategy covering safety, substance, timing, method, location, data and QA/QC.
Monitoring data will be used for regulatory purposes
Use an effective QA/QC system to obtain high-quality results and remove invalid data.
A new periodic monitoring campaign is carried out
Review the monitoring strategy for each campaign.
A periodic monitoring campaign is planned
Document the campaign strategy in the site-specific protocol.
A pollutant can exist in more than one physical phase
Select a method that measures the required phase or all relevant phases.
Missing a material phase of the pollutant
A stable emission is measured periodically
Normally take at least 3 consecutive samples of at least 30 minutes each.
Too little evidence for a stable emission
A periodic instrumental technique is used on a stable emission
Allow one continuous sample of at least 90 minutes as an alternative to three 30-minute samples.
Fragmented sampling where continuous evidence is suitable
A manual method cannot meet its analytical detection limit in 30 minutes
Increase sample duration enough to meet the laboratory LOD.
Reporting a result below method capability
Dioxins or furans are measured periodically
A single 6-to-8-hour test may replace the general minimum of 3 tests.
Applying the generic three-test rule incorrectly
Emissions are unstable or highly variable
Increase the number of samples or follow the permit-specific requirement.
Manual sampling could be contaminated during preparation, transport, installation or analysis
Use field blanks as a quality-control check.
Handle it like the measurement series near the sample location but do not draw stack gas through the equipment.
Turning a blank into a real sample
A field blank result is evaluated
Treat a blank at or below 10% of the ELV as generally acceptable, subject to the applicable standard.
A CEN method field blank has a measurable value
Do not deduct the field blank value from the sample result.
